identified_factors: Disabled tractor-trailer is blocking the right lane
Incident is on I-4 eastbound, a major interstate
Location is near Exit 55, which may affect merging and exiting traffic
recommended_actions: Verify the blockage and assess traffic conditions and queue length
Consider warning approaching drivers and providing temporary traffic control
Coordinate appropriate roadside assistance or incident response resources
Monitor for congestion growth and secondary crashes
missing_information: Whether the tractor-trailer is fully or partially blocking the lane
Extent of traffic backup and current travel speeds
Availability of a shoulder or alternate lane passage
Whether anyone is injured or otherwise in danger
Whether hazardous materials, fuel leakage, fire, or other hazards are involved
Weather, visibility, and time of day
Exact roadway direction/location relative to Exit 55
unsupported_assumptions: Traffic can safely pass in adjacent lanes
The vehicle is on the shoulder or has warning devices deployed
reasoning_summary: A disabled tractor-trailer blocking a travel lane on a major interstate presents a substantial traffic and secondary-crash risk. HIGH is appropriate based on the confirmed lane blockage, but the absence of information about injuries, hazardous conditions, and congestion limits confidence in assessing whether the incident is critical.
